title: Verify the Correlation Bound for Randomized Present S-Box Sharing
summary: A maximal absolute correlation of one quarter is verified for the randomized three-sharing; it remains unresolved whether this holds for every static-randomness choice used for second-order probing security.

formal_statement.body: The randomized three-sharing of the Present S-box component $G$ has been verified to have maximal absolute correlation $2^{-2}$. When randomness is used to make this sharing second-order probing secure, verify that the maximal absolute correlation remains $2^{-2}$ for every possible choice of the static randomness.

scope.domain: Linear correlation and probing security of randomized masked S-box sharings in symmetric cryptanalysis.
assumptions: Randomness is used to make the sharing second-order probing secure.
parameters: Static randomness, with every possible choice in scope
scope.unresolved_remainder: Verify that the maximal absolute correlation remains 2^{-2} for every possible choice of the static randomness.

citations.label: Cryptanalysis of Masked Ciphers: A not so Random Idea

progress.summary: The source reports a verified maximal absolute correlation of one quarter for the randomized three-sharing, then identifies re-verification for all static-randomness choices under second-order probing security as the open task.
citation_labels: Tim Beyne et al., Cryptanalysis of Masked Ciphers: A not so Random Idea
